name: Nous (Mind) as cosmic cause
plain_explanation: Anaxagoras said that a special, pure substance called 'Mind' set the universe spinning and is what makes living things different from dead matter, unlike everything else, which is mixed with everything else.
precise_definition: Anaxagoras's doctrine that mind (nous) is a substance distinct from and unmixed with all other matter, infinite and self-ruled, which enters into living things and is the source of all motion, originating a rotation that gradually spreads through the world, sending light things to the circumference and heavy things toward the center.
why_it_mattered: It marks the first attempt in the tradition Russell surveys to give a non-mechanical, quasi-teleological cause (mind) alongside or instead of purely material explanation, and it is a direct forerunner of Socrates's interest (via Anaxagoras) in mind as an explanatory principle, later developed very differently by Plato and Aristotle.
historical_origin: Developed by Anaxagoras in Ionia and during his years in Athens (c. 462-432 B.C.).
examples: Mind causing the original rotation that separates light and heavy matter
Mind as the differentiating factor between living and dead matter
objections: Aristotle and the Platonic Socrates both complain that Anaxagoras, having introduced mind, makes very little use of it, resorting to mechanical explanation whenever he can.
Aristotle points out Anaxagoras invokes mind as a cause only when he has no other explanation available.
competing_positions: The Atomists' fully mechanical account of motion and vortex-formation, explicitly contrasted by Russell as an advance over explaining vortices by 'the action of mind'
influence_on_later_thinkers: Socrates professed to have learned from Anaxagoras the idea of the pre-eminence of mind in creation, though he was later disappointed (per the Phaedo, referenced by Russell's broader discussion) that Anaxagoras did not use mind to explain things teleologically.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Anaxagoras's naturalistic claims (sun as a red-hot stone, moon as earth) were the basis of his prosecution for impiety under a law targeting those who taught theories about 'the things on high.'

evolution.treatment: Anaxagoras said that a special, pure substance called 'Mind' set the universe spinning and is what makes living things different from dead matter, unlike everything else, which is mixed with everything else.
